mainTopic: Why a reed mat (מפץ) can get מדרס טומאה even though it cannot be purified in a מקוה; רבא's source that a כלי חרס cannot get מדרס; and the start of the משנה about planting five kinds of seeds in a small garden bed.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that uses a קל וחומר to show that a מפץ (reed mat) becomes impure from a מת. The גמרא challenges a hidden assumption in that ברייתא. A זב's bed only gets מדרס if it can be purified in a מקוה, so how can a מפץ get זב impurity at all? רבי חנינא answers that it is enough if items of its kind can be purified in a מקוה. After a sharp exchange with another sage, this is proven from two verses. One verse compares the bed to the זב, and the other includes every bed. רבא then gives a different source for why a כלי חרס never gets מדרס: the verse about a sealed vessel in a tent with a מת. That verse calls the sealed vessel pure even if it was set aside for a נדה. A new משנה then asks for the hint that five kinds of seeds may be planted in a garden bed of six by six טפחים, and it points to the plural word זרועיה in ישעיהו. The גמרא explains how רב יהודה counts the growing-words in that verse to reach exactly five.

steps.title: The ברייתא's logical argument that a reed mat becomes impure from a corpse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses a קל וחומר: small earthenware pitchers are not affected by a זב but do become impure from a מת. So a מפץ, which is affected by a זב, should surely become impure from a מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical: small pitchers are pure with regard to a זב, yet they are impure from a מת. A mat is impure from a זב, so isn't it logical that it should be impure from a מת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that proves a מפץ becomes impure from a מת. This is setup. The next step will challenge the hidden assumption that a מפץ gets זב impurity at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר works because מת impurity is broader than זב impurity. Even small pitchers, which a זב cannot make impure, still get מת impurity. The key hidden premise is that a מפץ CAN become impure from a זב, and that premise is what the גמרא attacks next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it is logical.' This introduces a קל וחומר argument.
A mat woven from reeds or similar plant material
A man with a certain bodily discharge who causes impurity, including through sitting or lying (מדרס)
A corpse, the most severe source of impurity

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is about whether a mat gets מת impurity in this discussion. The גמרא only cares about the premise hidden inside it: that a mat gets זב impurity.

phrases.english: And it is logical:
phrases.notes: This kicks off a קל וחומר argument.

phrases.english: Just as small pitchers
which are pure with regard to a zav
phrases.notes: They are not used for sitting, and they are too small to be touched inside

phrases.english: are impure from a corpse,
a mat, which is impure from a zav,
is it not logical that it should be impure from a corpse?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא about the מפץ that began in the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מפץ, which gets זב impurity, gets מת impurity by קל וחומר from small pitchers.

steps.title: But a mat cannot be purified in a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a מפץ would get זב impurity at all. It cannot be purified in a מקוה, and the rule was that only items that can be purified in a מקוה get מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why should it be impure from a זב? It cannot be purified in a מקוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's assumption that a mat gets זב impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא learned that a זב's bed is compared to the זב: just as he can go to a מקוה, his bed must be something that can go to a מקוה. A מפץ, as the גמרא understands it here, cannot be purified in a מקוה, so it should not get מדרס.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But why?' Here it is used to challenge.
Purification by immersion in a ritual bath

phrases.english: But why?
It has no purification in a mikveh!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי, הָא לֵית לֵיהּ טׇהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the hidden premise of the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's assumption that a מפץ becomes impure from a זב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule that a bed must be purifiable in a מקוה to get מדרס seems to exclude the מפץ.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: it is enough that its kind can be purified
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers that the מפץ is different. Other items of its kind, made from plant material, can be purified in a מקוה, and that is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said to him: It is different there, since items of its kind can be purified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא resolves the challenge by changing how the rule is measured. The question is about the item's category, not only about the item itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'it must be purifiable in a מקוה' is now read as 'its kind must be purifiable.' A מפץ belongs to a family of materials, like wood and plant vessels, that can go into a מקוה. So it qualifies even though this particular item cannot.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said to him:
It is different there
since there is purification in its kind.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the rule's scope, from the item itself to its category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only an item that can itself be purified in a מקוה gets מדרס.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is enough if items of its kind can be purified in a מקוה.

steps.title: Sharp rejection: may Heaven save us from this view
steps.stepSummary: The other sage strongly rejects רבי חנינא's idea that the category is what counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: May the Merciful One save us from this opinion!
steps.whatsHappening: The other sage (some identify him as רבי אילא) rejects רבי חנינא's answer with strong language.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He feels that saying 'its kind' counts has no basis. The comparison of the bed to the זב seems to require that the item itself can go to a מקוה. No reason is given here. It is a gut-level rejection that pushes רבי חנינא to bring a source.

keyTerms.meaning: May the Merciful One save us

phrases.english: He said to him:
May the Merciful One save us from this opinion!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea that 'its kind' is enough.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No explicit flaw is given. He implies the idea has no source and contradicts the comparison of the bed to the זב.

steps.title: רבי חנינא turns it around: save us from YOUR view
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers back that it is the other sage's view that is mistaken.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, may the Merciful One save us from your opinion!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא throws the rejection back. This sets up the next step, where the reason for his view is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying 'אדרבה,' רבי חנינא claims his opponent's view is the one that goes against the Torah. The proof itself comes next.

phrases.english: On the contrary,
may the Merciful One save us from your opinion!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The opponent's view that only the item itself counts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The flaw is explained in the next step: that view ignores one of two verses.

steps.title: Two verses that seem to pull in opposite directions
steps.stepSummary: The reason for רבי חנינא's view is given. There are two verses: one compares the bed to the זב, and one includes every bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Two verses are written. It is written, 'And a man who touches his bed,' and it is written, 'Every bed that the זב lies on shall be impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two verses are brought as the basis for רבי חנינא's view. The next step will show how they fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse puts the bed next to the man (the זב). That is the source for 'just as he can go to a מקוה, so must his bed.' The second verse says 'כל המשכב,' every bed, which sounds like it includes even beds that cannot go to a מקוה. Both verses must be given a meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: A bed or anything used for lying on

phrases.english: And what is the reason?
Two verses are written.
It is written: 'And a man who touches his bed,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:5. The bed is compared to the זב himself.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'Every bed'
that the zav lies upon shall be impure.'
phrases.notes: The word 'every' includes even beds that can't be immersed in a מקוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the textual basis for רבי חנינא's position.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's rule that 'its kind' is enough.

steps.title: Reconciling the verses: its kind decides
steps.stepSummary: If items of its kind can be purified, the bed is impure even though it cannot be purified itself. If its kind cannot be purified at all, the comparison to the זב excludes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If its kind can be purified, it is included even though it cannot be purified in a מקוה itself. If its kind cannot be purified, the verse compares his bed to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how both verses work together, and this proves רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Every bed' includes items like the מפץ, whose category can be purified. The comparison to the זב excludes things like כלי חרס, whose whole category can never be purified in a מקוה. So the earlier rule still stands, and the מפץ is an exception that the Torah itself includes.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? How do these fit together?

steps.whatToRemember: For מדרס, the question is whether the item's KIND can be purified in a מקוה. A מפץ qualifies. A כלי חרס does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why כלי חרס is exempt from מדרס while many non-immersible plant-based items are not.

phrases.english: How so?
If there is purification in its kind,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ טׇהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶה.
phrases.english: even though it itself has no purification in a mikveh, it is impure.
If there is none in its kind,
the verse compares his bed to him, and it is excluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension between the two verses brought in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An item gets מדרס if its kind can be purified in a מקוה, even if it cannot be purified itself. If its kind cannot be purified, it is excluded.

steps.title: רבא's different source: a sealed earthenware vessel stays pure
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a new source that a כלי חרס cannot get מדרס. It comes from the verse about a sealed vessel in a tent with a מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: That מדרס does not apply to a כלי חרס is learned from here: 'Every open vessel that has no sealed cover on it' is impure. This implies that if it has a sealed cover, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different source for the rule that a כלי חרס does not get מדרס. This sets up his proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about a tent with a corpse in it says an open vessel becomes impure. By implication, a כלי חרס with a tight seal stays pure. רבא will next show why this implies there is no מדרס for earthenware.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity caused by a זב or נדה sitting, lying, or leaning on an item

phrases.english: Rava said:
That an earthenware vessel is pure from treading-impurity is learned from here:
'And every open vessel'
that has no sealed cover on it,' is impure
this implies: if it has a sealed cover on it,
it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִדְרַס כְּלִי חֶרֶס טָהוֹר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the exemption of כלי חרס, instead of the comparison of the bed to the זב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מדרס does not apply to a כלי חרס, learned from the verse about צמיד פתיל.

steps.title: Even if set aside for a נדה, the sealed vessel is pure
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the verse includes a vessel designated for use by a נדה. Since the Torah still calls it pure, it never got מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we not also dealing with a case where he set it aside for his wife while she was a נדה? And still the Torah says it is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא completes his proof from the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כלי חרס could get מדרס, a vessel used for sitting by a נדה would already be impure, and the seal would not help. The Torah calls every sealed vessel pure without any exception. That shows earthenware is never made impure by מדרס.

keyTerms.meaning: Are we not dealing with a case where
He designated or set them aside
A menstruating woman, who causes מדרס like a זב

phrases.english: Are we not dealing with a case
where he designated it for his wife who is a niddah,
and still the Torah says it is pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּיַחֲדִינְהוּ לְאִשְׁתּוֹ נִדָּה
steps.raayaObject: The rule that מדרס does not apply to a כלי חרס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The general wording of במדבר י״ט:ט״ו, which includes even a vessel designated for a נדה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: a sealed כלי חרס is pure even if it was set aside for a נדה. This proves earthenware has no מדרס.

steps.title: New משנה: five seed types in a six-by-six garden bed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks for the source that one may plant five kinds of seeds in a garden bed of six by six טפחים: four along the sides and one in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: From where do we know that in a garden bed six by six טפחים, one may plant five kinds of seeds in it, four on the four sides of the bed and one in the middle?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks for the source of a כלאים rule about planting several kinds of seeds in a small bed. This sets up the verse in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה continues the chapter's pattern of הלכות hinted at in פסוקים. The question is how mixed planting can be allowed in a small area without breaking the איסור of כלאים. The arrangement, four on the sides and one in the center, keeps each kind separate enough.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about planting on שבת. It is a כלאים rule, brought here only because it is hinted at in a פסוק, like the other rules in this section.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
From where do we know regarding a garden bed
that is six by six handbreadths
that one may plant five kinds of seeds in it,
four on the four sides of the garden bed
and one in the middle?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לַעֲרוּגָה שֶׁהִיא שִׁשָּׁה עַל שִׁשָּׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a 6×6 טפחים bed, five kinds of seeds may be planted: four on the sides and one in the middle.

steps.title: The verse says 'its seeds,' in the plural
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings ישעיהו's verse 'and as a garden makes its seeds grow.' It points out that the plural 'זרועיה' is used, not 'זרעה,' hinting that several kinds grow in one small garden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'For as the earth brings forth its growth, and as a garden makes its seeds grow.' It does not say 'its seed' but 'its seeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the פסוק that hints at the rule from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on one word. 'זרעה' would mean one kind of seed, while 'זרועיה' means many kinds. The plural hints that a small garden can hold several kinds of seeds at once.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not say this, but rather that

phrases.english: As it is said: 'For as the earth brings forth its growth,'
'and as a garden causes its seeds to grow' —
'its seed' is not said,
but rather 'its seeds.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי כָאָרֶץ תּוֹצִיא צִמְחָהּ וּכְגַנָּה זֵרוּעֶיהָ תַצְמִיחַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the question asked in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that five kinds of seeds may be planted in a 6×6 bed.
steps.whatToRemember: The plural 'זרועיה' (seeds) hints that several kinds may grow together in one small garden bed.

steps.title: Where does the verse show five kinds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking how the verse quoted in the משנה shows that five kinds of seeds may be planted.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: How do we learn this from the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking how the verse actually teaches the number five. This sets up רב יהודה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה showed that the plural word זֵרוּעֶיהָ means more than one kind of seed. But a plural only proves 'at least two,' not 'five.' So the גמרא asks where the full number five comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that follows the משנה
How is this implied? Where do we see it?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the משנה. The גמרא agrees with the rule of five kinds. It only wants to see how the verse produces that exact number.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: This is where the גמרא starts discussing the משנה.

phrases.english: From where is it implied?
phrases.notes: It asks how the verse shows five kinds, not just 'more than one.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details behind the proof from the verse that the משנה brought in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the verse in ישעיהו shows exactly five kinds of seeds.

steps.title: Counting five from the words of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה counts the growing-words in the verse and reaches five: תּוֹצִיא (1), צִמְחָהּ (1), זֵרוּעֶיהָ (2), תַּצְמִיחַ (1).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The verse says 'For as the earth brings forth its growth.' 'Brings forth' is one. 'Its growth' is one. That makes two. 'Its seeds' (plural) is two, so now there are four. 'Makes grow' is one more, so there are five.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by counting words in the verse that refer to planting and growing. Each word stands for one kind of seed, and the total is five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He goes back to the full verse that the משנה quoted (כִּי כָאָרֶץ תּוֹצִיא צִמְחָהּ וּכְגַנָּה זֵרוּעֶיהָ תַצְמִיחַ). The משנה had used only the plural זֵרוּעֶיהָ, and now he counts every growing-word in the verse. The singular words תּוֹצִיא, צִמְחָהּ, and תַּצְמִיחַ each count as one. The plural זֵרוּעֶיהָ counts as two, because a plural means at least two. Together they add up to exactly five, which matches four seeds on the sides of the bed and one in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings forth. Counts as one kind.
Its growth or vegetation. Counts as one kind.
Its seeds. It is plural, so it counts as two kinds.
Makes grow. Counts as one kind.
That makes. Used here to give the running total.

steps.whatToRemember: The verse in ישעיהו has five 'units' of growing: תּוֹצִיא (1) + צִמְחָהּ (1) + זֵרוּעֶיהָ (2) + תַּצְמִיחַ (1) = 5. This hints that five kinds of seeds may be planted in a garden bed of six by six טפחים.
steps.confusionAlert: זֵרוּעֶיהָ counts as two, not one. That is because it is plural, and a plural always means at least two. If you count it as one, you will only get four.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the source for the rule of five kinds in one bed. The source is only a hint (זכר לדבר). It is not the real origin of the law of כלאים.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
"For as the earth brings forth its growth"
phrases.notes: The start of ישעיהו 61:11. The משנה quoted the whole verse but only used זֵרוּעֶיהָ; now רב יהודה counts all the growing-words.

phrases.english: "Brings forth": one,
"Its growth": one. That makes two.
"Its seeds": two. That makes four.
phrases.notes: It counts as two because the word is plural.

phrases.english: "Makes grow": one. That makes five.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כִּי כָאָרֶץ תּוֹצִיא צִמְחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By counting the growing-words in the full verse: 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 5.
steps.raayaObject: That five kinds of seeds may be planted in one small garden bed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 61:11: כִּי כָאָרֶץ תּוֹצִיא צִמְחָהּ וּכְגַנָּה זֵרוּעֶיהָ תַצְמִיחַ
